page: Microsoft Azure D16_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a nominal base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 64.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 foundation instructions, AVX-512 VNNI, AES encryption, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. This specific instance size includes no local ephemeral storage and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network-attached disks for storage requirements.

Benchmark evaluations position the D16_v4 primarily within the middle tier of general compute instances. Multi-core compute benchmarks such as Geekbench (7,938) and PassMark CPU (15,671.52) demonstrate steady multi-threaded capacity, supported by a stress-ng multi-core result of 14,885.14. Single-core performance leans weaker, as indicated by a lower-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 1,412.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,269.0. Memory throughput tests show predictable uncached read bandwidth of 82.97 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 45.16 GB/sec. The system handles memory-centric workloads effectively, recording 13.89 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 12.04 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure perspective, the D16_v4 delivers balanced resource allocation without the added overhead of bundled local SSD storage. This design presents a cost-effective operational profile for architectures that separate compute logic from persistent data tiers. However, workloads dependent on ultra-low disk latency or high single-thread clock speeds may encounter bottlenecks. The instance is suited for multi-threaded application tiers, static web servers, distributed caching nodes, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and relational database servers backed by managed network block storage.

Delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64.0 GB of system memory, it features a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions, but lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark results consistently place the instance in the middle tier for multi-threaded tasks, memory bandwidth, and static web serving, while single-core compute performance sits in the lower percentile. Operating without ephemeral disks, the D16_v4 provides an efficient resource footprint for multi-tier web applications, Redis caching nodes, microservice orchestration, and general enterprise workloads utilizing decoupled block storage.
